Hi Priya / Rahul 

Great to meet you today  thanks for the time. Quick recap from our discovery + the follow-ups I promised:

1) High-level recommendation (based on the use cases you described: clinical triage + summarization):
   - Strong contender (best quality): Llama 3 13B (FP16)  highest quality on instruction-heavy prompts for clinical summarization.
   - Cost/throughput balance: Mistral Instruct 7B (int8)  good quality for retrieval-augmented workflows and much better throughput per GPU.
   - Low-cost/embedding-heavy / high TPS: Redwood-Opt-13B quantized (8-bit)  lower latency per token but watch for prompt-specific regressions on succinct clinical phrasing.

2) Redwood-verified performance profiles (quick snapshot for the configs we typically benchmark):
   - Llama3-13B (FP16) on A100-40GB: p50 latency = ~28 ms/token, p95 = ~110 ms/token (32-token generation). Sustained TPS (concurrent short prompts) ~140 r/s.
   - Mistral-Instruct-7B (int8) on A10/T4 class: p50 = ~45 ms/token, p95 = ~200 ms/token. TPS ~70 r/s.
   - Redwood-Opt-13B (8-bit) on A10: p50 = ~55 ms/token, p95 = ~240 ms/token. TPS ~48 r/s.

Notes: these numbers are Redwood-verified on our public benchmark harness with simulated concurrency and representative short/medium prompt mixes. Real numbers on your workload will vary with prompt length, retrieval latency, and batching strategy.

3) Quality/regression concerns:
   - Aggressive int8/4-bit quantization can introduce subtle generation differences on clinical shorthand and tokenization edge cases. We recommend running your prompt set and key evaluation slices (edge cases + safety prompts) before committing to a quantized variant.

4) Deliverables I'm attaching / linking:
   - Attached: acme_prompt_set_v1.csv (sample prompt set you shared) [Attachment: acme_prompt_set_v1.csv]
   - Benchmark dashboard (Redwood): https://redwood.app/benchmarks/llama3-13b-acme
   - Shared report (PDF): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/acme/model-fit-report [will attach full PDF in next email]

5) Proposed next steps / mutual action plan:
   - You: confirm a 12k sample of high-priority prompts & the key evaluation metrics you care about (ROUGE / clinical fidelity / hallucination tolerance).
   - Us: run a tailored benchmark (quality + perf) across 3 model candidates with your prompt set and return a short report. Target turnaround 4872 hours after we receive the sample.
   - Schedule: 3045m deep-dive to review results + recommendation. I suggested Wed 3pm PT but open to alternative times.

If that all sounds good I will kick off the tailored runs once you confirm the sample and give us S3/Drive access (or you can upload to the shared Drive link).

Cheers,

Thanks Priya  quick answers inline and attaching the full PDF bench report.

- Cost delta (ballpark, per 1M output tokens, hosted pricing proxies; final costs depend on batching and reserved capacity):
   - Llama3-13B (FP16): ~$1,800$2,400 / 1M tokens
   - Mistral-7B (int8): ~$650$950 / 1M tokens
   - Redwood-Opt-13B (8-bit): ~$450$700 / 1M tokens

  Note: Dedicated/Reserved capacity commitments can materially reduce per-token costs (we can run numbers for a 12-month commit).

- Examples of quantization regressions: we typically see shorter, factual answers truncate or change punctuation on 4-bit extremely aggressive configs; in clinical prompts that manifests as tokenization artifacts on abbreviations (e.g., "hx" -> expanded inconsistently). We'll include 2 redacted examples in the attached PDF.

- Private + KMS: yes  Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and can integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or on-prem HSMs. We can review the compliance checklist during the deep-dive.
